quizName: DMV Practice Test #13 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: To reduce your reaction time to a hazard, you should:

options.text: Always ride under the speed limit.
Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
Shift into neutral when slowing down.
Pull the clutch when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: In dangerous areas like school zones or construction zones, keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes. This lets you react faster to a hazard.

questions.question: When a group of motorcyclists enters a highway or takes a curve, they should:

options.text: Ride single-file.
Ride in a staggered formation.
Ride in pairs.
Ride in the far right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride single-file.
questions.explanation: Staggered formation is usually best, but switch to single-file when turning, taking curves, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: When you park a motorcycle next to a curb, it should be:

options.text: Parked at a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
Parked at a 45-degree angle with the front tire touching the curb.
Parked like a car, with the front and rear wheels the same distance from the curb.
Parked at the left edge of the parking space so drivers can see it easily.

questions.correctAnswerText: Parked at a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
questions.explanation: Park your motorcycle at a 90-degree angle to the curb with your rear wheel touching the curb.

questions.question: When you are stopped, you should:

options.text: Stay in first gear.
Stay in neutral.
Stay in fifth gear.
Stay in any gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in first gear.
questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears as you slow or stop. Stay in first gear while stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Always stay in one part of the lane and never move from it.
Change your lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
Only ride in the center of the lane so other vehicles see you.
Ride in a zigzag pattern so drivers notice you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: There is no one lane position that is always best. Change your position as needed based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: When being passed, do not move to the far side of your lane because:

options.text: The passing vehicle may return to your lane too soon.
You may block another vehicle from passing you.
The side closest to the passing vehicle is better.
You are more likely to feel a wind blast from the passing vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The passing vehicle may return to your lane too soon.
questions.explanation: Do not ride on the far side of your lane when being passed. This may tempt the other driver to return to your lane before it is safe.

questions.question: When a vehicle on your left is passing you, you should:

options.text: Move as far to the right as possible to help them pass.
Move to the shoulder to help them pass.
Ride in the center portion of your lane.
Ride in the left portion of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center portion of your lane when being passed. Riding too far right increases collision risk. Riding too far left may tempt the driver to return to your lane too soon. Stay centered.

questions.question: The best lane position:

options.text: Is always the right portion of the lane.
Is always the center portion of the lane.
Is always the left portion of the lane.
Changes based on road, weather, and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Changes based on road, weather, and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Change your position based on road, weather, and traffic conditions.

questions.question: If your front tire locks while braking, you should:

options.text: Keep the brake engaged until you stop completely.
Release both brakes and coast to a stop.
Release the front brake and use only the rear brake.
Release the brake lever until the tire grips the road again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the brake lever until the tire grips the road again.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks while braking, release the brake lever until the tire regains traction, then reapply the brake.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Help you see and be seen.
Keep you away from other drivers' blind spots.
Avoid surface hazards.
Block your escape route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Block your escape route.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see and be seen, avoids other drivers' blind spots, and avoids surface hazards. It should discourage other drivers from sharing your lane and provide you with an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: A person with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of ______ or higher is legally intoxicated.

options.text: 0.02 percent
0.04 percent
0.08 percent
0.1 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent
questions.explanation: A person age 21 or older with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is legally intoxicated. It is illegal and unsafe to drive any vehicle while intoxicated.

questions.question: Motorcycle headlights are:

options.text: Usually more powerful than car headlights.
Usually as powerful as car headlights.
Usually less powerful than car headlights.
Usually larger than car headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually less powerful than car headlights.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle headlights are smaller and less powerful than car headlights.

questions.question: You may need less extra space between you and the car ahead if:

options.text: The road is slippery.
You cannot see past the vehicle ahead.
Weather and traffic conditions are perfect.
Traffic is heavy.

questions.correctAnswerText: Weather and traffic conditions are perfect.
questions.explanation: Increase your distance from the car ahead when conditions are not perfect. Keep extra space if the road is slippery, you cannot see past the car ahead, or traffic is heavy.

questions.question: The best straight-line braking is done by:

options.text: Using the front brake first, then the rear brake.
Using the rear brake first, then the front brake.
Using both brakes at the same time without locking either wheel.
Using both brakes at the same time while locking the rear wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using both brakes at the same time without locking either wheel.
questions.explanation: The best straight-line braking uses both the front and rear brakes together without locking either wheel.

questions.question: When riding in a group, motorcyclists should:

options.text: Spread out so others can see the group better.
Stay close together so others can see the group better.
Separate from time to time.
Ride in pairs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay close together so others can see the group better.
questions.explanation: Riders in a group should stay close together while keeping enough space to move safely around each other. This makes the group easier to see and keeps riders from getting separated. Pairs do not leave enough room to maneuver.

questions.question: A rectangular sign is usually a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limit signs are rectangular with white background and black lettering. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT affect blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: The amount of alcohol consumed
How quickly the alcohol is consumed
The person's body weight
How often the person drinks alcohol

questions.correctAnswerText: How often the person drinks alcohol
questions.explanation: Three main factors affect BAC: the amount of alcohol consumed, how quickly it is consumed, and the person's body weight. It is illegal and unsafe to drive while under the influence of alcohol.

questions.question: At minimum, how often should you check a motorcycle's hydraulic fluid?

options.text: Once a day
Once a week
Once a year
Before every ride

questions.correctAnswerText: Once a week
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before each ride for safety. Check hydraulic fluids and coolants at least once a week.

questions.question: If you brake while turning a curve:

options.text: Only use the front brake.
It is the same as braking on a straight road.
You will have more traction as you lean.
You may have less traction as you lean.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may have less traction as you lean.
questions.explanation: You can use both brakes while turning, but you must be careful. When leaning to turn, some tire grip is already used for the turn, so less grip is available for braking.

questions.question: When riding, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your arms straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn just your head and eyes to look through turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head and eyes to look through turns.
questions.explanation: When turning, look ahead to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level.

questions.question: When riding at night, a motorcyclist should maintain a minimum following distance of:

options.text: Two seconds.
Three seconds.
Four seconds.
Five seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Three seconds.
questions.explanation: At night, it is harder to see and judge distance. Keep at least three seconds between you and the vehicle ahead. You need extra time to see that they have stopped and to slow down or stop safely.

questions.question: Motorcycle riders:

options.text: Should wear hearing protection at all times to prevent hearing damage.
Should only wear hearing protection during long rides.
Should not wear hearing protection because it will muffle other noises, such as horns and sirens.
Do not need to use hearing protection if they are using a helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should wear hearing protection at all times to prevent hearing damage.
questions.explanation: Wind and engine noise can cause permanent hearing loss, even with a full-face helmet. Ear plugs protect your hearing and still let you hear important sounds like horns and sirens.

questions.question: If a friend has been drinking and wants to drive, which of the following should you not do?

options.text: Encourage friends to talk them out of driving.
Arrange for other transportation.
Tell them to take less-crowded roads.
Slow their pace of drinking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell them to take less-crowded roads.
questions.explanation: Do not let them drive. Instead, arrange another way for them to get home, get other friends to help stop them, or keep them busy to slow down their drinking. Never suggest they just take quieter roads.

questions.question: When selecting a helmet, make sure it is all of the following, except:

options.text: Designed to meet U.S. Department of Transportation standards.
Snug.
Defect-free.
Attractive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Attractive.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation and state standards. It should fit snugly and have no damage like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps. Appearance is not important for safety.
